key_insight: LoRA can be treated as a controllable probe for exact parametric memory, and the paper identifies a robust power-law relationship between memory gain, effective parameters, and sequence length.
engineering_relevance: The results provide a quantitative rule for allocating fine-tuning budget more efficiently when updating LLM knowledge, especially under tight compute or memory constraints.
method: Use LoRA as a controlled memory-capacity probe in latent space.
Fit a Parametric Memory Law linking loss reduction (ΔL) to effective parameters and sequence length.
Design MemFT to shift training toward sub-threshold tokens using a prediction-probability threshold.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic quantitative analysis at both sequence and token levels, including a deterministic phase transition and empirical evaluation showing improved memory fidelity and efficiency with MemFT.
watch_item: The p > 0.5 greedy-decoding threshold and the observed law may depend on model, data, and finetuning setup, so transferability should be validated before deployment.
paper_title: How LoRA Remembers? A Parametric Memory Law for LLM Finetuning
